items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: and Sylvia Cuenca who was Clark’s drummer for years who lived there, and John Allred on trombone who had just moved to New York

ctx.x: Oh well the three biggest mentors in my life I said one was Don Jacoby and Stan Kenton and Clark Terry. And it was funny because we were playing Wichita Jazz Festival, I think this would have been 1970 maybe, and Clark’s band opened for the Kenton band. His quintet. And so after the concert Stan and Clark are talking and Stan says, “I want to meet your lead trumpet player.” I mean Clark says, “I want to meet your lead trumpet player.” So Stan introduced Clark and I which became the friendship for the rest of the…

“I Got Rhythm” changes with just a few minor additions to the changes. But the joke was that you’re supposed to play it as fast as you can and I named it “Creepin’ with Clark” because no matter what the tempo was it didn’t matter to Clark. It was like nothing mattered to him, it didn’t matter how fast you went. And so I wrote that tune in honor of him. So we had talked for quite a few years about oh wouldn’t it be fun to do an album together. And we got an angel that put up the money and we recorded it at SONY…
Am I correct that you were at his bedside near the end of his life?
